title: Catalyst, reimagined.
subtitle: A clearer path to your next semester
narration: Catalyst, reimagined, is a student portal redesign by Aayush Keshari, Nipun Chandra, and Shivam Kharangate. This guided walkthrough uses captured states from the working prototype, with synthetic narration. The focus is finding classes and knowing when enrollment is complete. Every student record and registration action is fictional. The dashboard brings the next semester, academic essentials, and a current schedule into one workspace.

title: Find the right class.
subtitle: Search, filter, and keep your context
narration: The classes workspace connects discovery and registration. A student can search by course code, title, or instructor, including a code with spaces. Common filters cover subjects, open seats, format, and meeting days. Each section shows its instructor, meeting time, location, and availability. Search context stays with the selected student and semester, so returning to the search does not mean starting over.

title: Compare your options.
subtitle: Useful differences, side by side
narration: A comparison view makes section differences visible without navigating away. Here, two User Interface Design sections meet on different days and at different times. The comparison also shows credits, seats, instructor, and prerequisites. Students can compare up to three sections. Adding a selection to the cart is explicitly planning. It does not reserve a seat or complete enrollment.

title: Recover with a next step.
subtitle: Specific errors preserve the student’s plan
narration: In this captured review, Senior Design section one and UI Design section one overlap. The prototype names the conflicting class and explains how to recover by choosing another section. Confirmation is disabled, and no classes are enrolled. The same validation layer checks prerequisites, registration status, duplicate courses, seat availability, holds, and the credit limit. Replacing UI Design with section two resolves this conflict.

title: Know when you’re enrolled.
subtitle: A clear confirmation, then an updated schedule
narration: Once the selection is valid, the student reviews and confirms the complete enrollment. A receipt records the semester, time, course sections, and credits. This is the explicit transition from planning to confirmed enrollment. The schedule updates immediately. A failed review leaves the selection unchanged. Waitlisting remains a separate status and never implies enrollment. Dropping a confirmed class requires confirmation and offers immediate undo.

title: Keep the bigger picture clear.
subtitle: Earned, underway, and future credits stay distinct
narration: Academic progress separates earned credits from current coursework and future registration. The senior sample profile has ninety six earned credits, fifteen in progress, and fifteen remaining after this term, assuming those current courses are passed. The student can review a synthetic transcript, use a graduation checklist, and download a readable summary. An advisor must confirm actual requirements and final eligibility.

title: A useful experience, on any screen.
subtitle: Mobile agenda, accessible states, and honest evidence
narration: On a narrow screen, the schedule becomes an agenda with meeting details still available. Academic services groups support destinations, while tasks and preferences stay local to each demo profile. The case study explains the source review, background research, design decisions, and implementation. Twenty one behavioral tests pass. Real student feedback is still needed, and no participant results or measured usability improvements are invented. Explore the working prototype to try the complete workflow.
